primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Loss of the mesenteric fat pad after substantial weight loss can narrow the aortomesenteric angle, compressing the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery anteriorly and the aorta posteriorly and causing proximal obstruction.
vignette: A 19-year-old woman has early satiety, postprandial epigastric pain, and recurrent bilious vomiting after losing 14 kg during treatment of a chronic illness. CT of the abdomen shows dilation of the stomach and proximal duodenum with abrupt narrowing of the third portion of the duodenum where it passes between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: Median arcuate ligament syndrome involves compression of the celiac artery and does not produce the described third-duodenal obstruction between the aorta and SMA.
Nutcracker syndrome involves compression of the left renal vein between the SMA and aorta, classically causing hematuria or gonadal venous symptoms.
Annular pancreas is a congenital ring of pancreatic tissue around the duodenum and is not caused by acquired loss of the aortomesenteric fat pad.
Gastroparesis causes delayed gastric emptying without the focal CT finding of third-duodenal vascular compression.
key_expl: Rapid weight loss can deplete the fat pad that normally maintains the angle between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery. The narrowed angle compresses the third portion of the duodenum, producing postprandial pain, early satiety, bilious vomiting, and proximal gastric/duodenal dilation.
objective: Recognize superior mesenteric artery syndrome as acquired compression of the third duodenal portion between the SMA and aorta after major weight loss.
clues: third duodenum compressed between SMA and aorta
